why: The student reads the semicolon in 'if (x > 0);' as if it were not there, so they treat println("positive") as the if body; Java makes it an empty statement as the then-branch, so 'positive' is always printed.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: The student skips over the lone ; and so commits the SemicolonAfterIfHeader error: in Java the ; is the whole then-branch, so the next println always runs.

The student correctly evaluates -3 > 0 as false.
The student does not see the lone ; as a full statement that ends the if, so the next println runs on its own in the normal order.
